purpose-statement.title: Purpose Statement
purpose-statement.body:
My purpose with this portfolio as an educator is to display all the skills and competencies learned to foster a dynamic, inclusive, historical  and student-centred environment . This portfolio encompasses teaching strategies and assessments that showcase the knowledge that was retained over this one-year programme. The intention of attaining these new strategies and skills were to educate and equip myself with the ability to encourage learners in the classroom. This teaching practicum helped me acquire the confidence needed to navigate the evolving education landscape due to technological advancement.

This programme and portfolio have allowed me as a student of education to think critically, make mistakes safely, and discover my own strong points, weaknesses and potential. All teachers contribute various special strengths and perspectives to the learning community and through the portfolio I can display some of my own contributions. My teaching purpose is to cultivate an environment of equal opportunities, kindness and safety in classroom where all voices are valued. Through games based learning and scaffolded instruction, I aim to create motivated and excited students and I hope to empower them to become confident critical thinkers, researchers and life long learners.

letter-to-self.title: Letter to Self
letter-to-self.body:
Dear Zoe,
I fell in love with history during high school. It was my favourite subject. I was always interested and intrigued by the major events in history and I always felt happy doing history. I still feel happy when I teach history. I genuinely love the field. My teachers in high school were excellent and my school had subject awards and I constantly topped history class and attained them. This ultimately led me to become a teacher as I decided to pursue history as my degree, and I signed up for teaching as I knew I would be happy teaching the subject.

I wanted to pursue my Postgraduate Diploma in Education, but I hadn’t been placed as a teacher as yet so I was advised to do my Master of Education. After I attained my master’s, I was told that it was useless without my Post graduate diploma in Education as that was the qualification I needed to be considered for any promotions. I was reluctant to do it but I knew I had to at this point otherwise all my previous struggles would have no meaning. So I quickly applied for the last year that it was available free. My husband also pushed me to do it. Even though the ability to get a promotion in my current school is very low. I hope one day to be able to teach at a school where I can grow and advance my career in education.

I hope to achieve by doing this programme the necessary skills to have a positive impact on my students education. I hope to gain new perspectives, new methods,  and to uncover the weaknesses in my teaching philosophy. I would like to improve and become the best possible teacher that I can be.

teaching-philosophy.title: Statement of Initial Teaching Philosophy
teaching-philosophy.body:
My purpose as an educator is to cultivate a dynamic, inclusive, and equitable classroom where learners are empowered to develop critical thinking and emotional intelligence. I personally believe that welcoming environment without fear, judgement and criticism provides the best setting for learning. The teacher as well as the classroom must have warm and open personality or atmosphere while still making classroom boundaries and rules known. Patience, empathy and understanding as a teacher I believe is crucial. I think that if a student feel understood or respected by you, they will in turn respect and listen to you.

Through game-based learning I hope to add to the way history and social studies are learnt and experiences. While I believe traditional learning techniques such as reading and note taking are valuable and irreplaceable learning skills especially for history, I also strongly believe that more learning strategies are needed. I observed that there are not enough learning activities and games in history and social studies. In teaching History and Social Studies, I use these games and activities to bring past struggles and societal systems to life, transforming students from passive listeners into active participants.

 Teachers have a large impact on their students and can affect and influence them for the rest of their lives. I am committed to scaffolding both cognitive and affective growth, guiding students to become resilient, socially conscious citizens who can collaborate effectively and question the world around them. With proper guidance, and motivation students can benefit tremendously.

As a history teacher I see myself as a time traveller guide or time wanderer guide. I believe it is my duty to help portray to students the importance of significant historical events. I believe that I must help students visualise, interpret and remember different critical points in history that still affect the world today. I believe I can help update and transform history using games-based learning.

caption-b.title: Section B Caption
caption-b.body: The Unit focuses on the theme of Caribbean Economy and Slavery from the History CSEC syllabus. The unit concentrates on guiding children through the experiences of the African during the middle passage and on the plantations. It also highlights the structure of the plantation system that the enslaved African would have laboured in.

tech-lesson-plan.title: Lesson Plan with Two Technology Tools

caption-c.title: Section C Caption
caption-c.body: Technological integration is crucial as it encourages student engagement, motivation and skills needed for 21st century development as technology is rapidly advancing. Through the use of bubbl.us students were able to create their own concept maps to assist with reviewing the topic of immigration. The implementation of the game of Jeopardy encourage students who never attempted in class to volunteer and answer questions.

caption-d.title: Section D Caption
caption-d.body: The performance task assessment consists of hands-on projects, labs, presentations, and creative outputs while traditional assessment requires answering questions.. Performance assessments help educators to expand the student's comprehension of academic material and the application of critical thinking skills. Instead of testing what a person remembers, it measures how well a person can use and apply what they know.

caption-e.title: Section E Caption
caption-e.body: The integration of history and economics was very beneficial for the history students as they were able to learn in depth about economics topics found in history. The economics teacher is more familiar with economics and was capable of providing explanations and giving perspectives that I may not have been able to. Students were able to see the overlap of different subject field and how they intertwine and function in our society. Students may have been able to realise that the importance and relevance of a subject field may not only be directly seen but can be found mixed with fields enhancing them.

caption-f.title: Section F Caption
caption-f.body: The purpose of a reflective summary in a portfolio is to critically evaluate personal growth, teaching practices, and learning experiences. It allows the students to fully understand appreciate what they gained from the programme and also shows the examiner what was learnt.

benefits-and-challenges-of-administering.title: Benefits and Challenges of Administering the Assessment

feelings.title: Feelings
feelings.body: My feelings during completing the portfolio were ones of being overwhelmed and frustrated at the amount of work required. However this gradually changed. I realised it was a summary or compilations of tasks that reflected some of the main topics and skills we learnt throughout the academic year. I gained an appreciation of the knowledge and skills learnt during my year in this programme.

impact-on-discipline.title: Impact on discipline
impact-on-discipline.body:
The greatest impact on my discipline would have been the teaching practicum. I believe that the experience and practice of teaching  in different schools and being evaluated on my teaching in front of lecturers has made me more confident and self-assured in my ability as a teacher. I believe that no amount of instruction can accommodate or replace the value of the teaching practicum and the process of preparing and experiencing teaching in other schools.

I understand now that teaching is not merely about passing on information to the students but it is also about student engagement and catering to their various learning abilities and needs.

continued-professional-development.title: Continued Professional development
continued-professional-development.body: I have already attained my Master of Education Concentration in Curriculum and I am uncertain of my academic future in education at this point. I hope I would gain the opportunity to make a greater impact on education beyond teaching but I am not certain what qualifications and what direction I need to take to find that path.  However I appreciated having the opportunity to refine and practice my unit and lesson planning skills and the chance to work and cultivate my teaching practice. I greatly enjoyed being able to conduct games-based research as I was able to create my own history games which very exciting.

philosophy-of-education.title: Philosophy of Education
philosophy-of-education.body: My initial philosophy of education has been affected by my participation in the Pedagogy as Process course in a variety ways. Once my teaching practice was very teacher centred and I have learned the importance and value of student centred learning.  I appreciated learning about scaffolding and how to guide students and allowing them to work through problems instead of simply showing them the entire solution.  The affective in my teaching and lesson plans have allowed me to ensure that I focus on engaging students feelings and emotions when teaching. This is extremely applicable in a subject like history which focuses on different topics and experiences of cruelty towards humanity such as wars, colonisation, slavery and indentureship.
